card.keepWhy: The worst thing is not the last thing.
sources: Luke 23:26 (Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, made to carry the cross behind Jesus)
Luke 23:34 (“Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing”; soldiers divide his garments by casting lots)
Luke 23:39-43 (one criminal: “Jesus, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.” “Today you will be with me in Paradise”)
Mark 15:33-34, 37 (darkness from the sixth hour to the ninth; “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”, the opening of Psalm 22:1; Jesus breathes his last)
Mark 14:50 (the disciples all left him and fled); Luke 23:49, 55 (his acquaintances and the women watching from a distance; the women see the tomb)
Cicero, Against Verres 2.5.165 (crucifixion “the most cruel and disgusting penalty”), behind shot 1
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized
check: Luke 23:34a (“Father, forgive them”) is missing from some early manuscripts; it is in most Bibles. Confirm it is fine to quote without a note.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever wondered why christians would choose a cross as their sign?
options: it is strange. that’s the right place to start.
good. let’s look at it together, slowly.
then today you’ll see it differently.

steps.line: In the Roman world, a cross wasn’t jewelry. It was a shameful death, kept for slaves, rebels and criminals.
Jesus was sentenced to die on one. A man coming in from the country, Simon of Cyrene, was made to carry the cross behind him.
steps.label: Luke 23:26

steps.q: On the cross, Jesus prays for the soldiers. What do you guess he asks God for them?
o: To show them who he is
steps.why: “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Only Luke records it, said while they were crucifying him.

steps.line: On the cross, Jesus prayed, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Below, the soldiers threw dice for his clothes.
steps.label: Luke 23:34

steps.line: One of the criminals beside him said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” Jesus said, “Today you will be with me in paradise.”
steps.label: Luke 23:42-43

steps.q: A dying criminal asks only to be remembered someday. What’s surprising about Jesus’s answer?
o: He asks the man to confess first
He tells him to wait for the last day
steps.why: The man asks for someday. Jesus answers “today,” with no conditions and no time left to make up for anything.

steps.q: Darkness covers the land from noon. Hours later, Jesus cries out a line from Scripture. What is he quoting?
o: A prayer said at every Passover meal
The first line of a psalm of lament
steps.why: Psalm 22 opens, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” and ends in trust. Mark gives it in Aramaic, and some bystanders thought he was calling Elijah.

steps.line: At noon, darkness came over the land. Jesus cried out, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” Then he died.
steps.label: Mark 15:33-37

steps.q: Mark says that as Jesus died, something happened in the Temple. What?
o: The Temple curtain tore, top to bottom
The Temple lamps all went out
The priests stopped the evening sacrifice
steps.why: The curtain hid the holiest place, where only the high priest went once a year. Many Christians read the tear as God’s presence opened to everyone.

steps.line: Most of his disciples had fled. But the women stayed, watching from a distance, and saw where he was laid.
steps.label: Mark 14:50; Luke 23:49, 55

say: here’s what i love. christians took the most shameful sign of their world and put it on their walls, because of what happened on it.
they believe jesus’s death was love going all the way down, forgiving even there. and they believe it wasn’t the end. the worst thing is not the last thing.

steps.q: Some churches show a crucifix, a cross with Jesus on it. Others show an empty cross. What might each be saying?
o: They disagree about whether he died
One stresses Good Friday, the other Easter
It’s mostly a matter of decoration
steps.why: The crucifix says: see how far love went. The empty cross says: he isn’t there anymore. Both hold Good Friday and Easter together.

today.say: next time you see a cross today, on a church, a necklace, a wall, stop for one breath and remember “father, forgive them.” say it for someone who hurt you, or just think it: your choice.
options: good. one breath is enough to start.
then they’re already in your prayer. that’s the hard part done.

tomorrow.title: The stone was already moved.
tomorrow.line: three women walk to a tomb at dawn, worried about something that’s already been taken care of.
